subject: Renewal: Dedicated GPU top-up & tokens/sec SLOs
messages:
From: Lorenzo Rossi <lorenzo@skyforge.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: SkyForge Ops <ops@skyforge.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: Dedicated pool expansion & throughput expectations

Hannah —

Thanks for the earlier conversations. As we approach our renewal window (May 1), we need to finalize the dedicated pool expansion and the tokens/sec guarantees that will be contracted. A few specifics on our side:

- Current baseline: 4 reserved A100s (shared across three API routes) with observed sustained throughput ~18M tokens/sec during peak daytime windows.
- Planned growth: we expect a 2.5x increase in steady-state generation volume over the next 12 months (marketing + new search feature).
- Requests: +8 GPUs to the reserved pool (to be A100 equivalent), a sustained pool-level throughput guarantee, and a short burst headroom guarantee for product launches.

We want SLO language that maps to measurable metrics (tokens/sec, 5-minute rolling windows, and defined measurement ingress points). We also want a fallback/failover plan if guaranteed throughput isn't met (e.g., automatic routing to hosted fallback model, prewarmed quantized variants, and documented credit events).

Can you send a proposed SLO clause and pricing for the +8 GPU top-up for a 12-month renewal? Also include lead time for provisioning and expected warmup behavior (KV cache, prefix caching) so we can align our launch schedule.

— Lorenzo
Lorenzo Rossi
VP Engineering, SkyForge AI
lorenzo@skyforge.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Lorenzo Rossi <lorenzo@skyforge.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated pool expansion & throughput expectations

Lorenzo —

Appreciate the details. Attached is a working proposal (Redwood_SF_Renewal_Proposal_v2.pdf) that covers: pricing for +8 A100-equivalent GPUs, a proposed tokens/sec SLO (sustained and burst windows), and operational fallbacks. Highlights below:

- Provisioning: 6–8 business days for dedicated capacity allocation in the us-west region, plus 24–48 hours for model warmup and prefix cache priming at your standard traffic patterns. We recommend a 72-hour ramp for large launches.
- Sustained throughput (contracted): 48M tokens/sec pool-level sustained, measured as a 5-minute rolling average across all routed requests.
- Burst allowance: 80M tokens/sec pool-level for a maximum continuous 5-minute window, 2x/day without penalty; additional bursts are subject to a grace policy.
- Measurement and telemetry: throughput measured at the ingress proxy (per-route token accounting), with transparent dashboards and daily sampling logs for SRE audits.
- Violation remediation: automatic routing to hosted fallback model variant (smaller quantized weights) plus a service credit of 3% of monthly reserved capacity fee per incident, up to 30%/month.

Questions for you: are you expecting the burst windows to be contiguous (single 5-minute windows) or spikier across multiple short bursts? Also confirm whether you require a hard SLA credit floor (we've seen customers ask for a higher cap for enterprise agreements).

I'll loop in Jordan for pricing options and longer-term uplift mechanics (tokens-based vs GPU-based commitments).

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Attachment: Redwood_SF_Renewal_Proposal_v2.pdf (PDF, 612KB)
From: SkyForge Procurement <procurement@skyforge.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lorenzo Rossi <lorenzo@skyforge.ai>, SkyForge Ops <ops@skyforge.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 08:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Dedicated pool expansion & throughput expectations — contract redlines

Hannah —

Thanks for the proposal. We reviewed the draft with legal and ops. A few redlines / asks before we can proceed to signature:

1) Throughput guarantees: we want the sustained tokens/sec number expressed as both pool-level and per-GPU-equivalent baseline. Proposed: 48M tokens/sec pool-level sustained, but please provide the equivalent tokens/sec per A100-equivalent GPU for transparency.

2) Measurement window: prefer a 1-minute and a 5-minute rolling window to capture both short spikes and sustained degradation.

3) Credits: we propose an initial 5% monthly credit per qualifying incident, with escalation to 7.5% for repeated incidents within a 30-day rolling period. Max cap 40%/month.

4) Burst behavior: we need a clearly defined burst exhaustion policy and a stated warmup latency for prewarmed caches. Also require a 24-hour notice for planned capacity maintenance that might reduce available tokens/sec.

5) Fallbacks: acceptable but request a contractual guarantee that fallback variants preserve contractual data handling (no external model routing outside our VPC for the duration of any fallback).

Attached are the marked redlines (SF_redlines_20270411.docx). Please provide a revised addendum that maps our redlines to your proposed SLO text.

Regards,
SkyForge Procurement
procurement@skyforge.ai
Attachment: SF_redlines_20270411.docx
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: SF renewal — finalize SLO text and fallback constraints

Team —

Looping internal owners to finalize language. Action items and proposed responses to procurement redlines below (we'll include these as tracked changes in the revised addendum):

- Per-GPU equivalent: compute and include an estimate using our kernel-selection model. Proposal: 6.0M tokens/sec per A100-equivalent sustained (48M / 8 GPUs) as the baseline; note this is an operational estimate, actual per-GPU performance varies with sequence length and model. Vivek: can you add a short explanatory clause about dependence on sequence length distribution and KV cache hit rate?

- Measurement windows: accept dual-window measurement (1-minute & 5-minute rolling). We'll define that a violation is declared only when both windows are below threshold for 2 consecutive checks OR when the 5-minute window is below threshold for the measurement period. This reduces noisy credits from transient jitter. Jordan: can you draft the precise metric math and the telemetry source (ingress proxy counter vs token-meter)?

- Credits & cap: counter-proposal: 4% per qualifying incident, escalates to 6% if two incidents occur within a 30-day window, cap 35%/month. Rationale: balances customer protection with avoiding outsized credits during platform-wide events. Marissa: confirm commercial acceptability and compute P&L impact for the 12-month term at proposed pricing.

- Burst policy & warmup: define burst exhaustion as sustained >burst limit for >5 minutes. We'll provide unlimited first two burst windows/day (per proposal) and charge overage at pre-agreed rate thereafter. Warmup: expected KV cache warmup 24–72 hours; we'll commit to targeted prewarmed prefixes if customer provides sample traffic for a 72-hour warmup window before major launches.

- Fallback locality: agree to keep fallback routing within the customer's VPC or to dedicated hosted nodes with equivalent data handling (no routing to third-party models). Legal will need to sign off.

I'll produce the revised SLO clause with Jordan's metric math and Vivek's technical caveat, then send to procurement w/ DocuSign link.

Thanks — Hannah

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: SkyForge Procurement <procurement@skyforge.ai>, Lorenzo Rossi <lorenzo@skyforge.ai>, SkyForge Ops <ops@skyforge.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Revised addendum — SF renewal (A100 top-up + tokens/sec SLO)

SkyForge —

Thanks for the feedback and patience. Attached is the revised addendum (Redwood_SF_Renewal_Proposal_v2.pdf, updated) and a redline response that maps your comments to the proposed SLO. Key items summarized: 

1) Sustained throughput: 48M tokens/sec pool-level (5-minute rolling avg) and an estimated 6.0M tokens/sec per A100-equivalent GPU (calculated as pool / committed GPUs). Both numbers will be measured from the ingress token counter.

2) Dual-window measurement: we will evaluate both 1-minute and 5-minute rolling windows. A qualifying incident requires either (a) both windows below the contracted threshold for two consecutive checks OR (b) the 5-minute window below threshold for the measurement period. The metrics math is included in Section 3.

3) Credits: 4% monthly reserved fee credit per qualifying incident, escalates to 6% for repeat incidents within 30 days, cap 35%/month. We believe this is a fair middle ground.

4) Bursts & warmup: burst allowance revised to 80M tokens/sec for a single 5-minute window, first two bursts/day are covered. Warmup behavior documented: KV cache warmup expected 24–72 hours; for high-sensitivity launches we will prewarm provided prefixes during a 72-hour scheduled warmup (customer provides traffic snapshot).

5) Data locality during fallback: we commit to fallback routing remaining within your VPC or to our dedicated hosted nodes that adhere to the same contractual data controls; no third-party model routing. Legal must sign the data handling addendum (attached).

Next steps: please confirm acceptance of the revised SLO language. If accepted, we'll issue the DocuSign packet and schedule capacity provisioning (lead time: 6 business days once countersigned + 48 hours warmup). DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABC-DEF-123

If you want a post-signature canary run with staged traffic to validate end-to-end latency and KV cache behavior, we can schedule a 72-hour window during your launch.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
